lines.japanese: 目をこすって見間違いじゃないか確かめた。
lines.english: I rubbed my eyes to make sure I wasn't seeing things.

lines.japanese: なんだこの光景はがくぶるぶる。ありえない組み合わせに、俺は他の生徒の影に隠れてこの異常事態を見守った。
lines.english: What the hell was I looking at? *Shudder shudder.* Faced with an impossible pairing, I hid behind the other students and watched the anomaly unfold.

lines.japanese: 「なー、ハリウッド。ちょっと男の意見聞きたいんだけどー」
lines.english: “Hey, Hollywood. I want a guy's opinion on something.”

lines.japanese: 「はァ、なんでもどうぞ。つまらない話なら答えないけど」
lines.english: “Huh? Sure, ask away. Unless it's boring.”

lines.japanese: 「萌えってなんなん」
lines.english: “What’s that whole thing about someone being so cute you just melt?”

lines.japanese: 「へェ、面白いこと聞いてくるじゃない。俺もいまその概念について、研究してたトコなんだ」
lines.english: “Huh. Now that's an interesting question. I was just researching the concept myself.”

lines.japanese: 「つっても悪ィけど、明確なお答えはできないなァ。一口にいやァ興味なんだろうけど、そこに好意だの倒錯だの色んな感情が混じってんだ。なあ、面白いよなァ。他の言語でも表す言葉がないんだぜ」
lines.english: “Sorry, but I can't give you a precise answer. If I had to sum it up, I'd call it interest—but affection, perversion, and all sorts of other feelings get tangled up in it. Fascinating, isn't it? No other language even has a word for it.”

lines.japanese: 「てことは他の日本語にあるように、海外に萌えって言葉が輸出される可能性もあるわけだ。それも趣き深いだろォ、もっとも感情なんて言葉にないものがほとんどだけどなァ」
lines.english: “Which means the Japanese name for it could catch on in other languages, like other Japanese words have. There’s something rather profound about that, wouldn’t you say? Then again, most feelings never find words at all.”

lines.japanese: 「余計な講釈はいいんだよ、だからなんなのか分かりやすく教えろよ」
lines.english: “Spare me the lecture. Just tell me what it means.”

lines.japanese: 「知るかバーカ」
lines.english: “Like I know, dummy.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょちょ、なんなんソレ。知らないくせになんでそんなエラソーなんだおっさん」
lines.english: “H-hold on, what the hell? If you don't know, why were you acting so damn superior, old man?”

lines.japanese: 確かに偉そうだ。俺は副委員長に少しだけ同情した。
lines.english: She had a point. I felt a flicker of sympathy for the deputy chairwoman.

lines.japanese: 「まあ一つだけ教えてやってもいいけど」
lines.english: “Well, there's one thing I could tell you.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、なに？　なに、教えてよ」
lines.english: “What? What is it? Tell me.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえに萌えは欠片もねえなあ」
lines.english: “You don’t have a shred of moe in you.”

lines.japanese: それが彼女にとって名誉なのかどうかは別として、副委員長はその場に立ちつくした。
lines.english: Whether or not that counted as an honor for her, the deputy chairwoman stood frozen on the spot.

lines.japanese: 本日、美空学園番長対決の決着。勝者、針生蔵人。
lines.english: And that settled today's clash of the Misora Academy bosses. The winner: Kurodo Hariu.

lines.japanese: 副委員長に心から同情したが、慰めてやろうとは思わなかった。
lines.english: My sympathy for the deputy chairwoman was heartfelt. I had no intention of consoling her.

lines.japanese: 「というわけで２２日の終業式までに提出物は必ず仕上げておくように」
lines.english: “So be sure to finish all your outstanding assignments before the closing ceremony on the twenty-second.”
“Bow.”

lines.japanese: 担任教師が出ていくのと同時に教室中の空気が弛緩する。
lines.english: The instant our homeroom teacher left, the tension drained from the whole classroom.

lines.japanese: 急いで予備校に向かう受験組もいれば、帰りに寄るファミレスの相談をしてる推薦組もいる。その中で一人足早に廊下に向かう女生徒がいた。
lines.english: Some of the students facing entrance exams hurried off to prep school. Others, already admitted by recommendation, debated which diner to stop at on the way home. Among them, one girl hurried into the hall alone.

lines.japanese: ていうか実は席が近いからずっと気にはなってたんだよな。なにやってんだあいつ。
lines.english: Actually, with her desk so close to mine, I'd been wondering about her for a while. What was she up to?

lines.japanese: 俺は掃除班の作業が終わるのを待って、四つの机を重ねあわせて自分たちの作業台を作った。
lines.english: I waited for the cleaning group to finish, then pushed four desks together into a worktable.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君どうするの今日どうするの作業するの今からやるの！」
lines.english: “Haneda what are we doing today are we working are we starting now!?”

lines.japanese: びっくりした。渡来も同じことを考えたみたいで自然と目が合った。
lines.english: That startled me. Watarai had apparently thought the same thing; our eyes met without a word.

lines.japanese: いつも無関心なハリュー・クロードの視線も留まってる。ペットボトルのキャップをきゅるっと回したあと、水が喉を下る音がした。
lines.english: Even the habitually indifferent Claude Haryu had stopped to stare. He twisted the cap off his bottle, and then came the sound of water running down his throat.

lines.japanese: 「今日はちょっと帰ろうかと思ったけど私いた方がいいよね、でないと作業進まないよね、だって私がいれば今日中に作業終わるかもしれないよ、いた方がいいよねそれとも帰る？」
lines.english: “I was thinking I might go home today but I should stay right otherwise the work won't get done and if I'm here we might finish everything today so I should stay right or should I go?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ……体調悪いなら帰った方がいいかもな」
lines.english: “Uh, well... If you're not feeling good, maybe you should go home.”

lines.japanese: まだびっくりを持続していた俺は素で親切な学級委員になってしまった。
lines.english: Still too stunned to put on an act, I became a genuinely considerate class representative.

lines.japanese: 「えーっでも私いた方がはかどるよ、やだ知らないの私の作業効率凄いよ全体としてマッスル上がるよ羽田比３．５倍は上がるよそんな私帰していいの、今ならまだ間に合うよどうする？　お願いしとく？」
lines.english: “What but I'm faster if I stay don't you know how efficient I am the whole team's muscle goes up I'm worth three and a half Hanedas and you want to send that home there's still time what'll it be want to ask me nicely?”

lines.japanese: 「あでも正直に言ってね、いた方がいいのにいない方がいいって言われても困るし、いない方がいいなんてありえないのにウソつかれても困るよねみんな困るよね今ちょっと私うざいよね、だったらゴメンね」
lines.english: “But be honest okay because it'd be a problem if you told me to leave when I should stay and obviously there's no way you want me gone so lying would just make trouble for everyone and I'm being kind of annoying right now aren't I so I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「ああじゃあ今日は帰って家で大人しく……」
lines.english: “Yeah, then maybe you should head home and take it easy today—”

lines.japanese: 「あーっ！　なにコレ渡来さん見てコレ、今年の体育祭の写真だよ。この時は歴史的快挙だったよね、私大活躍だったよね、未来永劫語りつがれるよね、銅像とか建ったらどうしよう今から建てる？」
lines.english: “Oh! What's this Watarai look at this it's from this year's sports festival that was a historic achievement wasn't it I was amazing they'll tell the story forever what if they build me a statue should we start now?”

lines.japanese: 写真のレイアウトをしようとしたハリュー・クロードの手から山科が紙面を引ったくった。
lines.english: As Haryu Claude tried to lay out the photographs, Yamashina snatched the page from his hands.

lines.japanese: 「おい糞うぜえなあこの女。なあ明日香、一発ブチ込んでいいか」
lines.english: “God, this woman is fucking unbearable. Asuka, mind if I lay her out?”

lines.japanese: 「だ、ダメだよ先輩、暴力はいかん！」
lines.english: “N-no, Claude! Violence is wrong!”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ先輩！　はいコレ貸してあげるから今聞いて！」
lines.english: “Exactly, Claude! Here, I'll lend you these, so listen to them right now!”

lines.japanese: ハリュー・クロードの顔面に何枚かのＣＤが押しつけられた。ここで我慢したあいつは偉いと思う。俺なら例え女と言えども、巴投げの一発や二発はかましてるかもしれない。
lines.english: Several CDs were pressed flat against Haryu Claude's face. I admired his restraint. In his place, woman or no, I might have treated her to a judo throw or two.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ロックバードのＣＤ」
lines.english: “Oh. Rockbird CDs.”

lines.japanese: 目の前にＣＤを山積みされた男は、それを手に取って確認すると無言で鞄の中に押しこんだ。相変わらずファンには甘いやつ。
lines.english: The man confronted with a tower of CDs examined them, then silently stuffed them into his bag. He was as soft on his fans as ever.

lines.japanese: 「さて、それじゃあ山科も満足したみたいだし、いい加減作業を始めるぞ」
lines.english: “Well, Yamashina seems satisfied. Let's finally get to work.”

lines.japanese: 「だね。あと少しで終わりだしね」
lines.english: “Yeah. We're almost done.”

lines.japanese: 「はいはーい！　じゃあ私渡来さんと一緒にやるー！　なにやるなに任せる？　私最強の駒だからねジョーカーだからね軍艦大和だからね、一番大事なところ任せた方がいいよ」
lines.english: “Me me! I'll work with Watarai! What are we doing what will you trust me with I'm your strongest piece your joker your Battleship Yamato so you should put me on the most important part!”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ山科に最重要任務を与える。この作文を出席番号順に並べておいて」
lines.english: “Then I assign Yamashina our most vital mission. Put these essays in order by student number.”

lines.japanese: 「おお、さすがは渡来。猿でも出来る作業をよく見つけたな」
lines.english: “Impressive, Watarai. You found a job even a monkey could do.”

lines.japanese: 「並べるの！　渡来さん分かってるぅ、それ私の一番の得意科目だよ整列乗車なんて私にかかれば剣光帽影だよ、『集合・整列・右へ倣うな』なーんてＫｕＲｉＹａも言ってるしね！」
lines.english: “Putting things in order! Watarai, you get me! That’s my best subject. When it comes to lining up to board, I can marshal people like an army! Even KuRiYa says, ‘Assemble! Fall in! Don’t fall into line!’”

lines.japanese: 「ああソレ、リリシストがバンド名義だから誰が書いてるかなんて分からねえぞ」
lines.english: “That one credits the band as lyricist. Nobody knows who actually wrote it.”

lines.japanese: 「やだ、知らないの！　ＫｕＲｉＹａで間違いないよ、だって確たる証拠があるからね。例え名前が載ってなくても私には分かるもん」
lines.english: “What you don't know!? It was definitely KuRiYa I have incontrovertible evidence and even if his name isn't printed I can still tell.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、確たる証拠ってなんだい」
lines.english: “Oh? And what might this incontrovertible evidence be?”
“A hunch!”

lines.japanese: 「ドラ一枚めくっておくか」
lines.english: “Shall I turn over a lucky tile while we’re at it?”

lines.japanese: 俺はかわいそうなハリュー・クロードのために最大級のフォロー（親切）を入れてあげた。
lines.english: For poor Claude's sake, I offered the strongest support I could muster. Purely out of kindness.

lines.japanese: 「おしまい！」
lines.english: “Finished!”

lines.japanese: 次の瞬間には、山科が作文を両手で撒きちらしていた。
lines.english: In the very next instant, Yamashina scattered the essays from both hands.

lines.japanese: 「やっぱり並べるのは私の仕事じゃないよね、もっと動きを要求される仕事ない？　ダンス的な？　カラオケ的な？　ああじゃあ私みんなのために応援歌うたうよもーチョー元気出るよやる気出てくるよ」
lines.english: “Actually arranging things isn't my job is there anything that needs more movement something dance-like karaoke-like oh I know I'll sing everyone a fight song you'll feel super energized and motivated!”

lines.japanese: 「なに、カラオケだと。それなら俺も蛎崎うにの『恋のサインカーブ』の振り付けを覚えたばっかりだ。一緒に歌わせろ」
lines.english: “Karaoke, you say? I just learned the choreography to Uni Kakizaki’s *Love’s Sine Curve*. Let me sing with you.”

lines.japanese: 俺は散らかった書類を拾いあげながらエアギターを披露した。
lines.english: I struck an air-guitar pose as I picked up the scattered papers.

lines.japanese: 「やだ、羽田君も歌う！？　じゃあじゃあ順番ね私あとでもいいよ、あとでも先に盛り上げとく？　盛り上げるなら私が御影クリヤの新曲歌えば鯛も平目も舞い踊るよ、みんなエビバディダンシングタイムだよ」
lines.english: “You'll sing too Haneda!? Then we can take turns I don't mind going later or should I get everyone worked up first if I sing Kuriya Mikage's new song the sea bream and flounder will dance everybody dancing time!”

lines.japanese: 「ほら渡来さんも座ってないでここでアゲとかないと辛いよ、夜から私と渡来さんのツインボーカルでストリートライブやる予定だからね、なんなら事務所に書類送っとく？　私と渡来さんなら天下取れるはず？」
lines.english: “Come on Watarai get out of that chair it'll be rough tonight if we don't get hyped now you and I are doing a twin-vocal street show should we send an application to an agency you and I could conquer the world right?”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと。こらぱね田、おまえも歌うなら私帰るけど」
lines.english: “The hell? Hey, Paneda, if you're singing too, I'm going home.”

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿者、これは山科に歌わせておいて、その隙に作業を終えてしまおうという作戦だということが何故分からん」
lines.english: “Fool! Why can't you see the plan? We let Yamashina sing and finish the work while she's distracted.”

lines.japanese: 「ああだったらァ、俺がエアドラムしてやってもいいけど」
lines.english: “Well, in that case, I wouldn't mind playing air drums.”

lines.japanese: 「先輩は本物！」
lines.english: “Claude, you play real drums!”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ渡来、協調性のないやつだな。既に会場は三対一だぞ」
lines.english: “Watarai, where is your team spirit? The vote in this room is already three to one.”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱりぱね田も本気だったんだね……」
lines.english: “So Paneda was serious too...”

lines.japanese: 「もう担当はほとんど決まってるから、渡来のパートはエアベースな」
lines.english: “Most of the roles are settled now. Watarai, you're on air bass.”

lines.japanese: 「認めない！　エアベースって二重の意味で空気だよ」
lines.english: “I refuse! Air bass makes me invisible twice over!”

lines.japanese: 「よーし、それじゃあ３－Ａ有志によるエアーバンド『ウイングバード』第一回音合わせを始めるぞ」
lines.english: “All right! The Class 3-A all-volunteer air band Wingbird will now commence its first rehearsal!”

lines.japanese: 「始まってるの！」
lines.english: “We're actually doing this!?”

lines.japanese: 「で、どうしても頼みたいことってなに？」
lines.english: “So what was this favor you absolutely needed?”

lines.japanese: 「うむ、実は人助けなんだ」
lines.english: “Indeed. It's to help someone.”

lines.japanese: 「人助け？」
lines.english: “Help someone?”

lines.japanese: 作業が終わりさあ帰ろうという段になって、昇降口で渡来を誘ってみた。俺の秘策には渡来の存在が欠かせないからだ。
lines.english: The work was done and we were about to leave when I asked Watarai for help at the entrance. My secret plan could not succeed without her.

lines.japanese: 「渡来に頼みたいのは俺とこれから電話するやつの仲を取りもってほしいんだ」
lines.english: “I want you to smooth things over between me and the guy I'm about to call.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ～……やだよそんなの、あとあと面倒くさそうだよね」
lines.english: “What? No. That sounds like trouble waiting to happen.”

lines.japanese: 「頼む、紹介してくれるだけでいい。俺のたった一人の親友なのに、話も出来ずに切られてしまうんだ」
lines.english: “Please. Just put in a word for me. He's my one and only friend, but he hangs up before I can get a word in.”

lines.japanese: 「で、私の知り合いなの？」
lines.english: “Do I know him?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。入院してるから電話しか連絡のとりようがないんだ」
lines.english: “Yeah. He's in the hospital, so the phone is the only way I can reach him.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、気は進まないけど、仕方ないなあ」
lines.english: “Hmm. I'm not thrilled about it, but I guess I have no choice.”

lines.japanese: 「素晴らしい！　ありがとう渡来、さすが海老の尻尾を食べられる女はやることが違う！　マーベラス！」
lines.english: “Marvelous! Thank you, Watarai. A woman who can eat a shrimp's tail simply operates on another level! Marvelous!”

lines.japanese: よしさっそく電話しよう、森里君の電話番号を呼び出して、と……。
lines.english: Good. Time to call. I brought up Morisato's number and...

lines.japanese: 「よし、任せた渡来」
lines.english: “All right. I'm counting on you, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: ぷっ　ぷっ　ぷっ　ぷっ
lines.english: Beep. Beep. Beep. Beep.

lines.japanese: ぷるるるるっ……
lines.english: Rrrring...

lines.japanese: 「ああもしもし？　またあんた？　ちょっとさあ、イタ電しつこくね？　いい加減にしねえとこっちもさあ――」
lines.english: “Hello? You again? Seriously, these prank calls are getting old. If you don't knock it off, I'm gonna—”

lines.japanese: 「もしもし？　私渡来って言いますけど……」
lines.english: “Hello? My name is Watarai...”

lines.japanese: 「へっ、女の子？　え、誰？　渡来って、渡来、渡来……」
lines.english: “Huh? A girl? Wait, who? Watarai... Watarai...”

lines.japanese: 「渡来さんっ！　美空学園の！？」
lines.english: “Watarai!? From Misora Academy!?”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう。こんにちは」
lines.english: “That's right. Hello.”

lines.japanese: 「どど、どうもっ。自分、森里和馬いいます。あ、電話かけてくれたんだから知ってるか。はは……あ、一年のころ同じクラスだったの覚えてるかな」
lines.english: “H-h-hello! I'm Kazuma Morisato. Oh, you called me, so I guess you know that. Ha ha... We were in the same class our first year. Do you remember?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、森里君。あはは、久しぶりだよね。入院してるんだって？　大変だね」
lines.english: “Oh, Morisato. Ahaha, it's been a while. I heard you're in the hospital. That sounds rough.”

lines.japanese: 「い、いや、そんな大変ってほどでもねーけど、なんつかいま元気になったってカンジ？　つか普段より力漲ってるっつの？」
lines.english: “N-no, it's not that bad. Actually, I feel great now, you know? Like I'm bursting with even more power than usual?”

lines.japanese: 「そか、それはよかった。あ、それで今日電話したのは、森里君に紹介したい子がいるんだけど……」
lines.english: “I see. That's good. Anyway, I called because there's someone I'd like to introduce you to...”

lines.japanese: 「俺に？」
lines.english: “Me?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ちょっと変わってるけどいい子だよ。ちょっと待っててね」
lines.english: “Yeah. A little strange, but a good person. Hold on a second.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ、マジで？　誰だろ、渡来さんの紹介っていうとＢ組の井上さんかな、それともＣ組の石田さん……」
lines.english: “Whoa, seriously? Who could it be? If Watarai's introducing us, maybe Inoue from Class B, or Ishida from Class C...”

lines.japanese: <8>\「俺でしたァー！！」
lines.english: “It was meee!”

lines.japanese: プツッ
lines.english: Click.

lines.japanese: 残念ながら切られてしまった。また次回の対策を練っておこう。
lines.english: Sadly, he hung up on me. I would have to devise another strategy for next time.
